policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere חַטֹּאתָיו is plural (Ncfpc/Sp3ms); ketiv חטאתו is singular (Ncfsc/Sp3ms); same lemma (2403 b) and suffix. The ASV opens the verse "for his sins which he sinned" — plural — and renders the unvaried singular of the same noun later in the same verse as "and in his sin which he did", so the number is visible in the English. The plural distinguishes the qere.

Here the number runs the other way: qere וּבְחַטָּאתוֹ is singular (C/R/Ncfsc/Sp3ms), ketiv ובחטאתיו is plural (C/R/Ncfpc/Sp3ms), same lemma (c/b/2403 b). The ASV reads "and in his sins wherewith he made Israel to sin" — plural — which is the ketiv, not the base qere. No note is mapped to the word; the wording alone decides it.

Qere וּבִשְׂגוּב and ketiv ובשגיב are the same proper name (lemma c/b/7687), tagged C/R/Np in both, differing only in the vowel letter: waw in the qere, yod in the ketiv. Unlike a purely defective spelling, the difference survives transliteration — the ASV's "his youngest son Segub" carries the qere's u, where the ketiv consonants would give Segib. The name distinguishes the qere.
